answer:
m-xylene (1,3-dimethylbenzene, CAS 108-38-3):

- Critical temperature Tc = 617.0 K (343.9 °C)
- Critical pressure Pc = 35.41 bar (3.541 MPa, about 34.9 atm)
- Acentric factor ω = 0.326 (sources give 0.326 to 0.331)

**Where the numbers come from.** I looked these up in the `chemicals` Python library (Caleb Bell), which brings together several published data sets. Here is what each one gives:

| Source | Tc (K) | Pc (MPa) | ω |
|---|---|---|---|
| IUPAC | 617.0 | 3.541 | n/a |
| Yaws | 617.0 | 3.541 | 0.327 |
| CRC Handbook | 616.9 | 3.540 | n/a |
| CoolProp (HEOS) | 616.89 | 3.5346 | 0.326 |
| PSRK | 617.0 | 3.546 | 0.331 |
| Passut-Danner | 617.05 | 3.541 | 0.3311 |
| NIST WebBook | 618.0 | 3.536 | n/a |

I also worked out ω from its definition, using the library's vapour-pressure data with the Tc and Pc above. That gave 0.3264, which agrees with 0.326. The Joback and Wilson-Jasperson estimation methods give Tc of about 625 K and Pc of about 3.59 to 3.62 MPa. Those are predictions from group contributions rather than measurements, so I did not use them.

These values match the commonly used set in Poling, Prausnitz and O'Connell, *The Properties of Gases and Liquids*: 617.0 K, 35.41 bar and ω ≈ 0.326 to 0.327. I took that from memory and did not check it against the book itself. All the other numbers above came from the library lookup.
